definitions.gloss: to beat down; to thrash; to pummel
definitions.explanation: To strike someone repeatedly and violently, knocking them down. Can also be used figuratively to mean thoroughly defeating someone in an argument, competition, or debate.

examples.japanese: {相手|あいて}を{叩|たた}きのめした。
{試合|しあい}で{叩|たた}きのめされて、{立|た}ち{上|あ}がれなかった。
examples.english: I was thrashed in the match and couldn't get back up.

examples.japanese: {議論|ぎろん}で{完全|かんぜん}に{叩|たた}きのめされて、{何|なに}も{言|い}い{返|かえ}せなかった。
examples.english: I was completely demolished in the argument and couldn't say anything back.

notes:
FORMS:
{叩|たた}く (to hit) + のめす (to knock down). The ～のめす suffix intensifies the action, implying the target is knocked flat. Compare {打|う}ちのめす, which has a similar meaning.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {相手|あいて}を{叩|たた}きのめす (to beat one's opponent down)
- {徹底的|てっていてき}に{叩|たた}きのめす (to thoroughly thrash)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {打|う}ちのめす: to beat down — similar meaning but uses {打|う}つ instead of {叩|たた}く; slightly more literary
- {叩|たた}く: to hit — basic action without the intensifying suffix
- ぼこぼこにする: to beat up — colloquial slang
